subject: RE: SLA discussion — weekend patch policy, escalation window, and escrow ask
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Derek Liu <derek.liu@catalysthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-11T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: SLA: weekend patch policy & escalation/escrow ask

Hi Derek / Amelia,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I’m sending the redlines that came out of our commercial + ops review and summarizing a few focused asks where we’d like alignment before legal does a final pass. Attached: Catalyst_MSA_redlines_v3.docx (highlights on pp.3-6).

Top asks from our side:
- Weekend patch carveout: Redwood requests an explicit emergency-patch carveout permitting security/critical-fix code pushes during a declared maintenance blackout, limited to fixes that meet our emergency criteria. We propose a 4-hour P1 response SLA for on-call during such events (definition in attached redlines).
- Escrow/maintenance exception: For rare, authenticated customer-initiated maintenance that would otherwise breach the uptime window, we propose a short-term "maintenance escrow" process (notice + post-event evidence) rather than automatic service-credit triggers.
- Credits cap: To preserve predictable economics, we propose a cap on monthly service credits tied to the order form (suggested cap: 30% of monthly recurring fee) and a staggered credit schedule for partial outages.

These are commercial compromises — if Catalyst prefers to keep the current broad blackout protections, we can instead restrict Redwood’s weekend patch rights to security fixes only and require 24-hr notice for non-urgent changes. Legal will inevitably want precise language, so I’m looping Rachel to shape final text.

Next steps: can we get Catalyst’s view on the emergency-patch carveout and the escrow concept by EOD Tuesday? If okay, Rachel will produce short contract language for review.

Attachments: Catalyst_MSA_redlines_v3.docx (docx, ~42 KB)

Best,

Naomi — thanks for the summary and the redlines. A few quick reactions from our side:

1) Weekend patches: Catalyst understands the need for emergency security patches but we’re reluctant to broaden vendor rights during scheduled blackout windows. Our goal is to protect production for critical patient flows.
2) Escrow idea: interesting, but our procurement will want firm SLAs and auditability — if Redwood proposes an escrow process, we need clear evidence requirements and a short appeal window.
3) Credits cap: not impossible, but we need examples of how that would apply for multi-region deployments.

We have procurement and legal review this week; I’ll push to get you a prioritized list of redline concerns by Wednesday COB. In the meantime, can you ask Rachel to draft the minimal carveout language (security-only + emergency criteria) so our counsel can react directly?

—Derek

Naomi — quick internal take before legal weighs in:

- Keep the emergency-patch carveout but narrow it to "Critical Security Fixes" as defined (active exploit or CVSS >=9) and require a documented rollback plan within 24 hours. That eases Catalyst’s production risk while preserving our ability to patch.
- Escrow process: make it a documented advisory route (notice with signed acceptance from customer ops) that pauses credit triggers for up to 72 hours while evidence is collected; after 72 hours, normal crediting resumes. That buys time for investigation but keeps incentives aligned.
- Credits cap: agree with Naomi’s approach but propose the cap be a % of fees per affected deployment/region rather than the whole contract.

I’ll coordinate with Ben to identify operational telemetry we can give as evidence (error traces, deployment logs). Rachel, can you draft two short alternatives (1: security-only carveout; 2: security + limited urgent maintenance escrow) so Derek has a simple binary to take to Catalyst counsel?

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-13T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: SLA: weekend patch policy & escalation/escrow ask

Team — drafting language now. High-level note and proposed snippets below; I attached a short SLA_summary.xlsx with credit math examples we can share.

Proposed snippet A (security-only carveout):
"Notwithstanding any scheduled maintenance blackout, Vendor may deploy emergency security patches solely to remediate an Active Exploit or a vulnerability with a Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) score of 9.0 or greater, provided Vendor (i) provides notice to Customer within two (2) hours of the change where feasible, (ii) documents the change and the vulnerability remediated, and (iii) provides rollback instructions and test results within twenty-four (24) hours."

Proposed snippet B (security + limited maintenance escrow):
"For non-routine, customer-impacting changes necessary to avoid imminent harm to Customer production, the Parties agree to an escrowed maintenance process: Customer will acknowledge the proposed change via designated contact, Vendor will provide contemporaneous operational evidence, and Parties shall mutually agree to pause automatic service-credit accrual for a period not to exceed seventy-two (72) hours while evidence is reviewed. If evidence is not provided within the review period, normal crediting will apply."

I recommend we send both variants to Catalyst counsel with short bullets on pros/cons. I can be on the call with Derek’s team tomorrow 10am PT if helpful. Once we have Catalyst’s preference I’ll prepare a single redline document and a short memo for procurement (include the SLA_summary.xlsx).
